## Q220 Adversarial Source/PIT Review — Worker Handoff

### Source-contract baseline (from provided artifacts)
- `automation/q220_fsn_schema_gate.py` inspects only the SEC FSN archive `2009q1_notes.zip`; it verifies member presence (`sub/tag/dim/num/txt/pre`) plus headers/samples, and emits `archive_sha256`.
- It is **schema-structure only** — no narrative text-block mapping, no presentation-role check, no amendment/extension/duplicate/period-unit-context alignment logic.
- The live SEC URLs in the scripts are **provisional operational telemetry only**; per the universal adversarial-source rule they are not durable historical source readiness. An immutable dated snapshot is required before candidate-specific PIT.

### Findings — failure modes with minimal deterministic falsifiers and exact artifacts

| # | Failure mode | Minimal deterministic falsifier | Exact artifact required |
|---|---|---|---|
| F1 | Text-block ↔ presentation-role mapping incomplete/mislabeled | Enumerate `txt` rows whose `label`/`role` cannot be matched to a `tag` presentation-tree node in the same vintage | Frozen archive snapshot SHA256 + `tag`+`txt` row manifest |
| F2 | Taxonomy-extension / custom-namespace drift | Emit per-filing set of `xmlns:` prefixes and extension taxonomy URIs; flag any filing whose set differs from the vintage mode | Namespace manifest CSV (filing, accession, prefixes, extension URIs) |
| F3 | Section identity instability | Hash each narrative section by frozen tokenization; detect sections that split/merge across amendments | Section-boundary manifest + amendment lineage |
| F4 | Amended-filing contamination | Map `10-K/A` → parent `10-K` accessions; verify Q220 uses only the amended vintage consistently | Amendment lineage map (accession, amended-form, parent-accession, acceptance date) |
| F5 | Future/current XBRL leakage into historical snapshot | For each historical filing, assert all fact periods end ≤ filing report date; flag any period > report date | Period/unit/context alignment table with violation count |
| F6 | Duplicate facts / unit-context conflicts | Count duplicate `(concept, unit, context, period)` keys per filing; flag >1 distinct values | Duplicate-fact key counts per filing |
| F7 | Representation mismatch proxies filing length / generic readability | Control: correlate narrative mismatch rate with filing word count/readability score on the frozen vintage; mismatch must survive the control | Length/readability control table (no performance ranking) |

### Counterarguments (to force falsification, not consensus)
- A complete `txt` table does **not** imply correct presentation-role mapping (F1).
- Extension namespaces may be stable by design; drift alone is not failure unless it breaks concept alignment (F2).
- The frozen 2009q1 vintage may not represent current SEC FSN schema; member names in the archive are part of the source contract but can drift (schema-version gate needed).
- Length/readability control (F7) is confounded by industry mix; must be stratified, not pooled.

### Concrete next actions
1. Freeze an immutable dated snapshot of the SEC FSN archive (SHA256 + UTC date) before any Q220 PIT.
2. Extend `q220_fsn_schema_gate.py` to emit artifacts for F1–F6 (namespace manifest, amendment lineage, duplicate-fact counts, period/unit/context alignment, section-boundary manifest).
3. Publish a deterministic narrative-tokenization spec and section-identity rule; gate Q220 on it.
4. Run the F7 length/readability control on the frozen vintage only; do not rank/select candidates by result.
5. Keep Q220 in **Lane B (Frontier Discovery)** until F1–F7 pass and the concept-freeze audit (Q104-style) covers Q220 narrative concepts; do **not** promote to Lane A formal readiness.

### Uncertainty
- Full Q220 narrative PIT design is not visible in the provided context; this review covers the gate script and candidate spec only.
- No performance evidence exists; nothing is validated or authorized.
- Live SEC endpoints remain provisional; vintage freeze is a prerequisite, not a formality.
